_doc: Inference engines beside llama-server (engines.py). Each is started on the first request to /engines/<name>/..., forwarded its own API (colibri: OpenAI-compatible /v1/...), and stopped after idle_stop_s without requests (0 = never). exclusive: the main llama-server is stopped before this engine starts, and this engine is stopped (after its running requests) before llama-server starts again - for engines that need the node's memory. {port} in cmd is filled with port. Any value may be ${ENV_NAME}, filled from the container environment; an unset name skips that engine with a log line. health: a GET path that answers 200 once the engine is ready, or tcp for an engine with a raw protocol (ready when its port accepts a connection). start_timeout_s: how long a start may take (a 500 GB model's dense part loading from disk takes minutes). Logs: MODELS_DIR/engines/<name>.log.

engines.name: colibri
engines._note: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (or any model colibri runs) from COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR. --ram is the RAM budget colibri sizes its expert cache from: leave room for the OS and LightRAG. Lossless: never add --topp or --topk (they change which experts are routed). --kv-slots N serves N conversations at once (each with its own cache); 1 keeps DSpark drafting on. The image needs the colibri build stage (see README).

engines.name: colibri_worker
engines._note: An expert worker for colibri's cluster mode: the coordinator (the colibri engine above, with CLUSTER_WORKERS=host:port,... in its env) keeps attention, routing and the KV state, and sends each layer's routed experts to the workers as one request. colibri has this for its GLM-5.2 engine; DeepSeek V4.1 needs the same port (the plan's first cluster step). Started through /api/engines/colibri_worker/start, not by requests. Not exclusive: a worker uses only its expert cache.
